summary:
All 11 characters from CONTRACT §3 are built, rendered and packed: player, fisherman, lumberjack, farmer, miner, hunter, villager_a/b/c, deer and boar. In total that is 1540 frames, each 128x128 with the anchor at (64,104), in the directions S/SE/E/NE/N. The style is soft, toy-like 3D chibi: about 2.5 heads tall and about 80 px on screen, with big round heads, dark dot eyes with a highlight, rosy cheeks and puffy fur trims. Every frame gets a soft 1px coloured ink outline, matching the outlined look of the reference and keeping the white parka readable on snow.
- The player is the chief from the reference: white parka, a huge puffy fur collar, hood down, brown belt, satchel strap and dark hair.
- Workers: the fisherman has a yellow raincoat, sou'wester and orange gloves. The lumberjack has red plaid, a beanie, a big brown beard and suspenders. The farmer is a girl with a straw hat, braids and green overalls. The miner has an orange hard hat with a glowing lamp, a moustache and a vest. The hunter wears a brown fur cloak with a bear-ear hood, a green tunic and a quiver.
- Customers wear the yellow, red and blue parkas: villager_a has the black bowl cut from the reference crowd, villager_b a cream beanie with a pompom and pigtails, villager_c an ushanka and a striped scarf.
- The deer is fawn-like with spots and small antlers. The boar is round with tusks and a bristle ridge.
Animations:
- Walk is a bouncy chibi waddle; carry holds both forearms out at chest height.
- Chop and mine have a wind-up behind the head, a fast hit and a recoil. Harvest is a squat-and-grab.
- Fishing is a cast with a live line and bobber that lands on the water, then reeling.
- The sickle cut is a low right-to-left sweep. The bow is drawn with a visible string and arrow, then released.
- Happy is a hop with arms up and ^^ eyes. The animals trot with diagonal leg pairs and have idles with breathing, a tail wag and an ear twitch.
All loops were checked numerically to wrap without a jump. Atlases are palette PNGs made with libimagequant at 256 colours, which looks the same as the originals at 3x zoom; character assets total 3.45 MB against an 8 MB budget. char_check.py reports 0 errors and 0 warnings across 1540 frame names (no frame touches the 128px edge). In a headless Chromium Phaser 3.90 test, every frame resolves and every animation plays in all 8 directions through flipX (docs/previews/char_phaser_smoke.png). Also produced: 9 portraits at 128x128, a 512x512 key art of the chief waving, and a flying-arrow sprite for the hunter.
contract_gaps: happy: the contract gives no repeat value. It is written as repeat -1 and is seamlessly loopable; its last frame is a neutral stand, so playing it once (repeat 0) also works.
Animals (deer, boar) use the same 128x128 frame and anchor [0.5,0.8125] as humans. The contract allowed a larger frame, but they fit.

Portraits and the 512 key art use a 15-degree UI camera instead of the 30-degree world camera, so faces read better. They are UI images; every world sprite uses bl_common's camera, PPU and lighting unchanged.
The hunter holds the bow in the RIGHT hand and draws with the left, so the bow faces the camera in E/SE/NE. Because the game mirrors SW/W/NW, handedness never shows.
Atlas PNGs are 8-bit palette images with alpha (libimagequant), while pack_utils writes 'format':'RGBA8888' into the JSON meta. Phaser ignores that field.

carryPoint is constant per direction, taken from carry_idle frame 0. carry_walk bobs the hands about 1-2 px, so the game may add a small matching bob. Villagers have no carry_idle but still get carryPoint (same arm pose).
extra_keys: characters.<key>.headTop: px offset from the anchor (negative = up) to the top of the head or hat in idle_S_0, for speech bubbles and emotes. Range is -81 to -90 for humans; deer -56, boar -43.

characters.<key>.anims.<anim>.impactPoint: {dir: [dx, dy]}, px offset from the anchor where the tool hits on impactFrame: axe blade, pick tip, sickle blade, bobber splash on the water (fisherman), arrow launch point (hunter), hands (harvest). Negate dx for SW/W/NW. Present on player chop/mine/harvest and every worker's work.

sprites.projectile_arrow: {atlas:'char_hunter', frame:'projectile_arrow', anchor:[0.5,0.5], kind:'fx'}. A 64x32 flying arrow pointing screen-right, about 45 px long. Rotate it to the flight angle and spawn it at hunter work impactPoint on impactFrame 5; the in-hand arrow disappears on that frame.
sprites.portrait_<key> and portrait_player_512 carry a 'notes' field
Frame 'projectile_arrow' is an extra frame inside char_hunter.json
regenerate:
cd /home/user/nurient/frost-village && /tmp/bvenv/bin/python tools/blender/char_render.py -- --chars all --samples 28 --portraits --keyart --force && python3 -m pip install imagequant && python3 tools/blender/char_pack.py && python3 tools/blender/char_check.py
# Takes about 12 minutes on 4 cores; roughly 0.2-0.5 s per frame. Without --force it resumes and skips frames already in /tmp/fv_cache/characters. Use '--meta-only' to recompute carryPoint/impactPoint without rendering. On a PC: blender -b -P tools/blender/char_render.py -- --chars player
notes_for_integrator:
Manifest: assets/characters/manifest.json follows CONTRACT §2/§3.
- atlases: char_<key> for all 11 keys.
- images and sprites: portrait_<key> for the 9 humans, plus portrait_player_512 and projectile_arrow.
- characters{}: each entry has atlas, frameSize [128,128], anchor [0.5,0.8125], dirs S/SE/E/NE/N, mirror {SW:SE, W:E, NW:NE}, frameName '{anim}_{dir}_{i}', anims (frames/fps/repeat, plus impactFrame and impactPoint where they apply), carryPoint, shadow, portrait, kind and headTop.
- fps follow the contract defaults: idle 6, walk 12, carry 12, work/chop/mine 14, harvest 10, happy 10.
- impactFrame values: player chop 5, mine 5, harvest 3; work: fisherman 4 (bobber lands), lumberjack 5, farmer 4, miner 5, hunter 5 (arrow release).
- carryPoint is the same for every human, as [dx, dy, behind]: S [0,-31,false], SE [12,-34,false], E [17,-40,false], NE [12,-46,true], N [0,-48,true]. Negate dx for the mirrored directions.
- shadow: humans [46,18], deer [56,22], boar [62,26]. Characters have no baked shadow.

Rendering notes:
- Frames already include a 1px soft ink outline, so do not add another. Portraits and key art have no outline and a transparent background.
- Trimmed frames rely on Phaser's sourceSize, so setOrigin(anchor) works directly; this was verified in Chromium.
- docs/previews/char_carry_check.png draws the props' item_fish_cooked stack at carryPoint in all 8 directions. The props items are big compared with a chibi body (a 4-item stack covers the face in S view), so I suggest scaling hand-carried stack sprites to about 0.55-0.65.
- Tools are drawn only during work, chop and mine. Harvest uses empty hands; the hands' position on the grab frame is its impactPoint.

Previews and build environment:
- docs/previews/char_* is 39 files, about 7.9 MB, mostly GIFs at 1.5x showing all 5 directions. Drop GIFs if repo size matters.
- Raw frames are cached in /tmp/fv_cache/characters, outside the repo.
- imagequant was pip-installed into the system python3. Without it, char_pack keeps RGBA atlases (about 10 MB total, over budget), because Pillow's own octree quantiser bands visibly on hair and parkas.
- I did not touch bl_common.py or pack_utils.py, and made no git state changes. __pycache__ is already gitignored.
